fixes.explanation: No guards and no tower in this verse. God says Shebna is chiseling a tomb for himself in the rock. The guards can keep their feet up, because this verse has no work order for them. Shebna's chisel is busy with his own resting place.

Not quite. The text doesn't say Shebna dies in the City of David. God says He'll sling Shebna into a wide land, and “There you will die…” (Isaiah 22:18). That's the place the verse gives, and I'm not going to guess past it.

Ring and chain? Ooh, fancy, I'll give you that. But the verse names a robe and a sash. God says He'll clothe Eliakim with Shebna's robe and tie Shebna's sash around him (Isaiah 22:21). No bling on this list, friend.

Sandals and staff, like Eliakim's headed out on a hike! But that's not the list. God says He'll clothe Eliakim with Shebna's robe and tie Shebna's sash around him (Isaiah 22:21). No sandals and no staff are mentioned.

Judah is right. God says Eliakim “…will be a father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.” (Isaiah 22:21). Father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and the house of Judah? Sounds like a job with no days off.

Ephraim walked into the wrong verse with total confidence, and I respect that. The verse says Eliakim will be a father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah (Isaiah 22:21). Ephraim isn't named here. Judah is the word that fills the blank.

False is right. God says, “What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.” (Isaiah 22:22). It works both ways, and nobody can undo what Eliakim does with that key. The key goes on his shoulder, and I can't even keep track of my spatula.

Firm is right. God says, “I will drive him like a peg into a firm place…” (Isaiah 22:23). A peg only works if it goes into something solid. Then the verse adds another picture: “…he will be a throne of glory for the house of his father.”

Hidden sounds like a great spot for the last cookie, but it's not the word in this verse. God says He'll drive Eliakim like a peg into a firm place (Isaiah 22:23). The picture is about how solid the spot is, not whether anybody can see it.

Shields, now that's sturdy thinking! But they aren't on the list. The text says they'll hang on him all the glory of his father's house, including the descendants and the offshoots (Isaiah 22:24). Sorry, palace guards, this peg isn't taking your gear.
